newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells HRK65 mln 91-day T-bills, rate drops.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells HRK65 mln 91-day T-bills, rate drops.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry said on Tuesday it had raised 65 million kuna through 91-day treasury bills at an auction.
The issued price rose to 97.036 percent from 96.861 two weeks ago, with the rate easing another 25 basis points to 12.25 percent after a 50 points drop at the last auction.
Bills are payable in two days and they mature on May 15.
Reuters clients are advised that data on page MFHT may be delayed due to a technical fault.
Bids totalled 85 million kuna, overshooting the target by 35 million, assistant minister Hrvoje Radovanic told Reuters.
He put the weighted bid price at 97.049 and interest rate at 12.07 percent.
Radovanic said the lion's share of the issue went to the banking sector and companies bought only 12.31 percent.
Foreign investors still have no direct access to auctions though they can bid through Croatian banks or buy T-bills from them in secondary trade, he said.
The ministry will next auction 100 million kuna worth of 42-day bills on February 18.
